3-add-a-face-detector-trained-on-anime-a.line: Drawn faces are missed at any size, which points at a training gap this attacks directly. Not yet judged.

why.impact: Drawn recall is 50% and flat cartoons 0%, so a detector that knows drawn faces is the biggest possible gain.
why.odds: Anime detectors exist, but gnomes, clay and flat cartoons are not anime and may still be missed, and the five face points may be lacking.
why.path: Idea 4 waits for it, and it tells whether size tweaks (idea 2) matter at all.

2-let-the-current-face-detector-see-draw.line: Still cheap, but idea 1 found large drawn faces are found no more often than small ones. Not yet judged.

why.impact: A win would need no new model, but it could only help part of the drawn styles.
why.odds: Within each drawn style bigger faces were not found more often, and clay faces much less often, so a larger size is unlikely to help.

5-check-whether-faces-of-the-same-drawn-.line: Tells whether found drawn faces will be any use for clusters and characters.

why.impact: If recognition fails on drawn faces, finding them still helps crops and thumbnails but not clusters or likeness.
why.odds: ArcFace was trained on real faces, so good separation of drawn characters is unlikely.
why.path: It can use idea 1's boxed set (picture set 40), so it does not wait for a better detector.

4-send-each-picture-to-the-photo-or-the-.line: Only worth doing once idea 3 has shown a drawn-face detector works.

why.impact: It decides how a second detector ships without hurting the 98% on photos, but adds nothing if idea 3 fails.
why.odds: The WD14 tagger or a CLIP check should tell photos from drawings well, but mixed styles are hard.
